title: The Flux Gate
summary: Turn a loop in a stream of field, mark the faces of a cube and find the net flux when the field grows.
subject: physics
concepts: Flux through a flat area, E A cos θ
Outward normal and the sign of flux
Net flux through a closed surface
Flux in a field that is not uniform
learningOutcome: The student can find the flux through a flat area at any angle, give the sign of the flux through each face of a closed surface, and find the net flux in a uniform and a non-uniform field.

levels.title: Tilt the loop
levels.adds: Baseline: the flux through a flat loop is Φ = E A cos θ (Ex 1.14). Turn the loop to reach a target flux.
hints: Φ = E A cos θ, where θ is the angle between the field and the loop’s outward normal.
Facing the field (θ = 0) gives the most flux; edge-on (θ = 90°) gives none.
Beyond 90° the field enters through the outward side, so the flux is negative.

levels.title: Faces of a cube
levels.adds: New idea: outward normals give each face a sign, and the net flux through a closed surface in a uniform field is zero (Ex 1.15).
hints: For each face, compare the field with the outward normal: along it means flux out (+), against it means flux in (−), square to it means zero.
Opposite faces have equal and opposite flux in a uniform field.
What enters a closed surface also leaves it, so the net is zero.

levels.title: Find the angle
levels.adds: Harder: work backwards from a target flux to the angle, including a negative flux (Ex 1.14 turned round).
hints: Rearrange: cos θ = Φ / (E A). Remember A is the side squared, in square metres.
A negative flux needs an angle between 90° and 180°.
Use the inverse cosine, and check the answer lies between 0° and 180°.

levels.title: Growing field
levels.adds: New idea: in a field that grows with x the near and far faces do not cancel, so the net flux is not zero (Example 1.10).
hints: Only the two faces square to the field carry flux; the other four are parallel to it.
The far face is at 2a where E = α√(2a); the near face is at a where E = α√a. Each has area a².
Net flux = far (out) minus near (in): a² α (√(2a) − √a).

misconceptions: Flux is largest when the field is parallel to the surface
The net flux through a cube in a uniform field depends on how it is turned
A field that is not uniform still gives zero net flux through any cube
